correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the argument in characteristic two. With s=x+y+z the equation is ws^2+xyz; the coprime coefficients in w give geometric integrality, and yz=xz=xy=s^2=0 leaves only [0:0:0:1]. The hypersurface is S2 and regular in codimension one, hence normal. On w=1 the Tjurina relations kill mixed monomials, identify one linear combination of the three squares and kill all cubics, so the degree dimensions are 1,3,2 and the length is six. Here the Jacobian ideal is that of the surface in the chart, including its equation; the ambient quotient by just the three affine partials would not give this length. The first strict transform has equation r^2+xt(r+1+t)=0 in the x-chart, and the reduced exceptional P1 has singular points precisely at t=0,1,infinity (use the y-chart for infinity). The local changes of parameters in the proof reduce each to uv+r^2=0 over F2. In coordinates where the old reduced exceptional branch is u=r=0, the v-chart of the node blowup has equation U+R^2=0, with new exceptional v=0 and old strict transform R=0. This verifies the transverse intersections; each exceptional conic is split. Adjunction on the ambient point blowups gives discrepancy 2−2=0 at each step, so curve adjunction gives four (−2)-curves. This proves the split D4 diagram and relative minimality, with no assertion about a Milnor number or a required finer subtype. An independent all-extension count projects from the singular point to P2: there is one lift per base point off s=0 (q^2 points), no lift on s=0 except at the three coordinate zeros there, and q lifts at each of those three. Adding the projection centre gives q^2+3q+1. Its resolution replaces one point by four projective lines with three pairwise transverse intersections, giving q^2+7q+1 and the stated zeta function. In characteristic zero the four affine sign choices (±2,±2,±2) with product 8 have nonsingular Hessian, and no point at infinity is singular. The supplied finite checker was inspected; the count and local conclusions here use algebra valid over every stated field, not a small-field replay.

value.rationale: This is the bad prime of the specified classical integral trace model, not an arbitrary small-field slice. The result identifies what replaces the four classical nodes, specifies the exceptional curves over the ground field rather than only geometrically, and gives the exact arithmetic change on resolving them. That complete bad-reduction datum is useful when comparing Fricke models or determining all-extension counts; the value is not assigned to the point-count simplification alone.
